correctness.rationale: Independently used the sum and divided difference of the swap equations. For a distinct pair with sum s and product p the difference gives p=(s-1)^2+1/eta; substituting into the sum equation gives -2(s-1)[eta(s-1)(s-2)+2]=0. The sum and difference equations together suffice for swapping. At s=1 the roots are real distinct iff eta>4. The other branch forces 1<s<2 and p=s(s-1)/2, giving discriminant s(2-s)>0 and (1-x)(1-y)<0, with positive roots and one root above 1. This gives 0/1/2/3 orbits on the four stated regimes, including one distinct external pair at the fold eta=8 and none from the repeated inner root at eta=4. The derivative product eta^2(1-s+p)(1-3s+9p) yields the stated inner and both external multipliers, including +1 at the fold. The minus multiplier exceeds 1 for eta>8; the plus decreases strictly from 1, reaching -1 at the only admissible root of 2 eta^2-13 eta-25=0, obtained by squaring with 8<eta<10. The inner multiplier has modulus <1 exactly for 4<eta<5. Maximizing x(1-x)^2 on [0,1] gives 4/27, consistent with the claimed phase-space limitation. Inspected the frozen symbolic checker and independently derived the identities; no reliance on samples or nonlinear attraction at neutral endpoints.
